candidates.label: rw
candidates.change: A and B: anchor recovery word. Init and worker 'stosw; dec di' -> 'stosw; stosw; sub di,3' so a second FF 1F sits at anchor+2 during dwell; worker 17->20 bytes; phoenix_init template copy mov cx,9 -> 10; B first-rebuild mov cx,8 -> 9 (rebuild must copy >= 20 bytes). DX/BP unchanged (DL=0). +1 turn per generation.

The +1 turn per generation re-phases every battle, so the diff is dominated by trajectory chaos.

candidates.label: rwt
candidates.change: rw plus timing compensation: A add sp,100h -> 0FCh and DX 4000h -> 4004h; B add sp,600h -> 5FCh and DX 2400h -> 2404h (trail one push shorter so every generation triggers on the same turn as base). Side effect found in trace: DL becomes 4, so a '00 10' (add [bx+si],dl) hit now adds 4 to the pointer cell and the recovery call jumps to anchor+4 -> this variant defeats the main recoverable case.

threatFindings.threat: Single-byte ModRM hit FF CC (dec sp) at anchor+1 is recoverable by a second FF 1F at anchor+2 (card premise)
threatFindings.evidence: Every FF CC anchor death in traces pkj3o / e85a / e1b9 (KosherCode x2, fisherEXE x3, theGlopyGng) comes from an odd-aligned CC CC word that also overwrites anchor+2, so execution hits INT3 at anchor+2 regardless. Same deaths persist identically (same round) in rwt trace fg6of. Also dec sp would misalign the trail by 1 byte/turn, so the rebuild would fail anyway.

threatFindings.threat: Harmless 2-byte overwrite of the anchor word (00 10 = add [bx+si],dl from CS=1000h dword bombs of HRZ_Underflow / OST_Gamma) falls through to INT3 at anchor+2
threatFindings.evidence: Death mode exists: pkj3o 1/161 (Underflow r1161, anchor 00 10, anchor+2 = init CC), e1b9/e85a traces 1 each (Gamma2). In rwt trace fg6of the same battle survives the hit (call via recovery word) but dies one round later at anchor+4 because rwt's DL=4 adds 4 to the pointer cell. rw (DL=0) should survive it but was not traced. Threat c3v6s vs real Gamma/Underflow: +0.003 n.s.; their team scores vs base only 0.017/0.05.
threatFindings.impact: about 0.6% of traced deaths; upper bound about +0.002/battle

threatFindings.threat: 00 1F / 10 1F hits (add/adc [bx],bl) at the anchor are recoverable
threatFindings.evidence: They corrupt the pointer cell low byte (A2h + C0h = 62h). fg6of: OpcodeHunter/OnlyCode r1841 and Underflow2 r314 survive one round longer via the recovery word, then jump to xx62 (CC) and die.
Recovery word does not apply: the trail overwrites anchor+1..anchor+4. FF A5 deaths 80 (pkj3o) vs 78 (fg6of).

threatFindings.threat: Recovery word introduces new self-harm or breaks rebuild
threatFindings.evidence: fg6of 163 deaths vs pkj3o 161, same death classes; many battles die on the identical round; screens near base (rwt -0.001). Rebuild with 20-byte worker and CX 9 works.
threatFindings.impact: no measured cost beyond timing chaos

recommendation: Do not promote either candidate. The card's mechanism is real but tiny: only about 1 of 161 traced deaths is a harmless 2-byte anchor hit with anchor+2 intact (00 10 from Underflow/Gamma), so the upper bound is about +0.002/battle, which field S cannot resolve. FF CC hits come as odd CC CC words that also kill anchor+2. If anyone revisits this, keep DL=0 (rw form). Timing compensation through DX (rwt) breaks the main recoverable case. The +1 turn per generation in rw only re-phases battles (screen -0.015, strong -0.076, multi -0.097, all n.s.). Card closed.
notes: Trace bytes[] start at logged IP-4. Logged IP is after the faulting instruction (fault+1 for CC). Helper: agent2/night/scratch/A018/faults.cjs.
